question: During which period of Indian history were the stupas of Sanchi and Sarnath built, reflecting its architectural style?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mauryan rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The stupas of **Sanchi** and **Sarnath** were constructed during the **Mauryan rule**, specifically under the reign of **Emperor Ashoka**, who ruled from **268 BCE to 232 BCE**.
 
• These stupas are among the earliest examples of **Buddhist architecture** in India and were built to enshrine relics of the Buddha and serve as sacred places of worship and meditation.
 
• Emperor Ashoka's patronage of Buddhism led to the construction of numerous stupas across India, including the famous Sanchi Stupa, which is now a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The architectural style reflects the influence of Mauryan art, characterized by intricate carvings, polished stone surfaces, and detailed relief work depicting scenes from Buddha's life and Jataka tales.
